description: We are Putumayo University, looking to connect, share, and exchange solutions from the Amazon.
summary: This website application was born from the necessity to reach farms that have a hard time accessing the information and technology resources, translating complex NASA data into a plan step by step to enhance production, maintain soil quality, and avoid diseases and pests of the cocoa plant, primarily in the Amazon region.
details:
This web platform, available as a downloadable app as well, guides farmers on topics related to cocoa production. It uses location to retrieve basic NASA data and other certified sources to generate a plan with different options that suit their needs.

This project has a social impact. This region has beeen suffered political conflict due to cartels and drugs; however, in recent years the community has been looking for other sources of income, like exporting Amazon fruits, vegetables, and others, especially cocoa. The goal of this model is to contribute to the success of these new sources of income.

To develop this website, we used TypeScript, JavaScript, React, and Next.js, with HTML and custom CSS for the interface. It uses Leaflet for interactive maps and GeoTIFF.js to read soil data. The platform retrieves climate data from NASA POWER and soil estimates from SoilGrids. It also includes features for saving and exporting plans, including PDF and CSV downloads.

Please check the following detailed information:

1. LANGUAGES AND FORMATS

TypeScript: Handles application logic, data validation, API queries, and statically typed components.

JavaScript / ES Modules: Powers the runtime environment and module system.

TSX / JSX: Used to build user interfaces in React.

HTML & CSS: Defines page structure, custom styling, responsive layouts, and print-ready views.

JSON: Manages data exchange, scenario exports, and climate data backups.

CSV: Enables downloadable agricultural log templates.

GeoTIFF: Processes geographic soil data retrieved from SoilGrids.

Markdown & TOML: Used for project documentation and deployment configuration.

2. FRAMEWORKS AND LIBRARIES

Next.js 16.4.5: Core framework managing pages, navigation, rendering, and API routes.

React 19.3.1: Builds interactive UI components, forms, and state management.

React DOM 19.3.1: Renders React components in the browser.

Leaflet 1.9.4: Powers the interactive map, coordinate selection, and farm plot location.

GeoTIFF.js (geotiff) 3.0.5: Parses geographic raster files from SoilGrids.

pdfmake 0.3.14: Generates and downloads customized farming plans as PDFs.

Lucide React 1.68.0: Provides UI icons.

Next.js features implemented:

App Router: Organizes screens and routing architecture.

Shared Layouts: Maintains a seamless flow across different screens.

Route Handlers: Manages server-side API endpoints.

next/navigation: Controls client-side navigation and redirects.

next/dynamic: Loads the interactive map strictly on the client side without server-side rendering.

next/image: Optimizes image rendering.

next/font/local: Loads self-hosted fonts locally.

Caching & Revalidation: Reuses external API responses to improve performance.

3. SERVER AND DEVELOPMENT TOOLS

Node.js 24.x: Runs the server environment, development scripts, and test suites.

npm: Manages package dependencies and script execution.

Webpack: Bundles assets during local development.npm run dev).

Turbopack: Compiles and verifies production builds.npm run build).

TypeScript Compiler (tsc): Performs static type checking without emitting build files.

Prettier: Enforces consistent code formatting.

@types/ packages:* Provide TypeScript definitions for Node, React, Leaflet, and pdfmake.

Git: Tracks version control.

GitHub: Hosts the source repository and deployment pipeline.

PowerShell: Runs CLI commands and local verification scripts on Windows.

4. DATA SOURCES AND EXTERNAL SERVICES

NASA POWER: Supplies historical and recent temperature, relative humidity, and precipitation data.

SoilGrids 2.0 (ISRIC): Provides soil pH and organic carbon estimates at a 5–15 cm depth.

OpenStreetMap: Serves map tiles for the base layer.

WCS 1.0.0: Protocol used to download SoilGrids geographic layers.

HTTP/HTTPS & JSON: Handles communication between external services and internal API routes.

Custom system endpoints:

GET /api/context: Fetches climate data from NASA POWER.

GET /api/soil: Retrieves soil estimates from SoilGrids.

POST /api/scenario: Evaluates farm conditions and generates tailored action plans.

5. BROWSER APIs AND FEATURES

Geolocation API: Detects the user's device location upon permission.

Fetch API: Executes network requests to the server.

AbortController & AbortSignal: Cancels pending requests and manages timeouts.

sessionStorage: Preserves active user progress during a browsing session.

localStorage: Saves generated scenarios manually across sessions.

Blob & Object URLs: Handles client-side file generation and downloads.

window.print(): Enables direct printing of farming plans.

Intl: Formats dates and numbers specifically for Colombian Spanish conventions.

6. DESIGN AND DATA VISUALIZATION

Custom CSS: Written from scratch without third-party frameworks like Tailwind or Bootstrap.

Custom Climate Chart: Built natively using React and CSS, without external charting libraries like Chart.js or Recharts.

DM Sans & Manrope: Self-hosted local fonts in WOFF2 format.

PNG & WebP: Used for interface images and logos.

Responsive Design: Adapts cleanly across mobile, tablet, and desktop screen sizes.

7. TESTING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

node:test: Runs automated test suites.

node: assert/strict: Validates test assertions.

Native Node TypeScript Runner: Executes tests directly without external testing frameworks.

npm run typecheck: Validates TypeScript types across the codebase.

npm run build: Verifies production build integrity.

(Note: 35 automated tests cover climate data, soil metrics, input validation, scenario logic, farming guides, and dosage calculations.)

8. DEPLOYMENT

Netlify: Configured via netlify.toml for hosting.

Netlify Next.js Adapter: Supports Next.js pages and server-side API routes on Netlify.

Netlify CLI: Documented as an alternative for deploying directly from the terminal.

Localhost: Runs locally at 127.0.0.1:3000.

(Note: While deployment configuration files are in place, this does not necessarily indicate an active public deployment.)

In conclusion, we consider connecting certified scientific NASA data and translating it into a tailored plan with multiple options, with language for people without technical expertise, presenting information relevant to each cacao farm can definitely contribute to economic growth and a positive social impact in the region, mainly in the Amazon region of Colombia.
